knowledge_gaps: The four-item mean loses ordering and explicit frequency information: one interaction and four identical interactions produce the same pooled embedding. It can represent recent composition, but does not reliably distinguish repeated interest from an isolated purchase.

The receptive-field claim needs correction. Adding raw four-position context takes the union of existing dependencies with offsets 0–3; it does not necessarily extend each block's dependency span by three positions.

No explicit comparison isolates the added context from the starting current-item gate or additional parameters. Any permitted comparisons must train separate single-model variants and never combine their predictions.

Reproduction remains incomplete: concrete block integration, optimizer registration after gate creation, embedding scaling/dropout conventions, predictor implementation, parity tolerances and remaining budget allocation are unspecified.

Originality 4 is plausible, but difficulty 3 understates integration and verification work. Potential 6 remains speculative: training mean rank 8.75 does not establish that recent-context gating addresses the observed ranking errors.

The new direct embedding paths bypass intermediate activation patches. Existing probes can remain valid sensitivity measurements, but their interpretation must explicitly account for these unpatched paths. Gate saturation and nearly constant gates also need measured diagnostics.
